amniotic mesodermal cells have the potential to be used as an alternative source for cell therapy in CF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

amniotic mesodermal cells are capable of differentiating into cells of the hepatic lineage and can be used for CFTR gene transfer to the respiratory epithelium, which could represent a new therapeutic approach in the treatment of cystic fibrosis.
hAMSCs have a potential to differentiate into hepatocytes and airway epithelial-like cells, and that the latter express the CFTR gene.
hAMSCs can be differentiated into hepatocyte-like and epithelial cells, including airway cells, which may be useful for cell therapy in CF and in other diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hAMSCs may be a new source of cells for CF gene and/or cell-based therapies, as well as a model for studying CF pathogenesis and for testing new therapeutic approaches.
the use of hAMSC-derived epithelial cells may represent a novel approach for the correction of the CFTR defect in the airway epithelial layer.
amniotic mesoectodermal cells can be differentiated into epithelial cells and that they may be useful for the development of novel therapeutic approaches for CF.
